What Does Anti-Graffiti Film Solve?

Glass Etching

Typical glass replacement after acid etching ranges from $800–$3,000 per panel depending on size and glazing type. Sacrificial anti-graffiti film takes the damage instead — peel and replace for $3–$8 per square foot. The glass underneath is untouched.

Spray Paint

Paint and permanent markers bond instantly to bare glass. Anti-graffiti film prevents adhesion — graffiti wipes clean with water and a cloth. No solvents, no scrubbing, no cleaning bills.

Sticker Buildup

Promotional stickers, political posters, and adhesive residue bond permanently to unprotected glass. Film provides a sacrificial surface — when covered, peel and replace.

Repeat Targeting

Vandals return to easy targets. A protected surface that cleans in minutes removes the incentive. Protected storefronts see repeat vandalism rates drop significantly.

Cleaning Costs

Commercial graffiti cleaning runs $150–$500 per incident. For high-frequency locations like transit stops and downtown retail, annual cleaning costs exceed film installation within months.

Sacrificial Barrier

Acts as a replaceable skin against spray paint, markers, and acid etching — saving your glass from permanent destruction.

Rapid Restoration

Damaged film is peeled away and replaced in minutes, costing a fraction of full glass replacement.

Optically Invisible

Maintains 100% clarity. Vandals won't even know the film is there until their damage fails to stick.

Two Types of Anti-Graffiti Protection

Sacrificial Film

Recommended for Glass

Clear polyester film applied directly to glass. When vandalized, peel and replace — the glass underneath is untouched. Cost: $3–$8 per square foot installed. Best for: storefronts, transit glass, school windows, entry doors.

Permanent Coating

Non-Glass Surfaces

Chemical coating for concrete, brick, metal, and signage. Graffiti removes with solvent cleaners. Multiple cleaning cycles before recoating required. Best for: walls, pillars, metal doors, concrete surfaces.

Anti-Graffiti Film FAQ

Does anti-graffiti film work against acid etching?

Yes. It's specifically designed to protect against acid etching, which permanently damages unprotected glass.

How often does the film need to be replaced?

Film is only replaced after an incident — otherwise it lasts 5–10 years. Many locations go years without needing replacement.

Can it be applied to mirrors and other surfaces?

We primarily install on glass surfaces. Contact us about specific surface types.

How long does anti-graffiti film last before replacement?

Undamaged film typically lasts 2–5 years in Arizona sun. When vandalized, only the affected panel needs replacement — not the full installation.

Can anti-graffiti film be combined with security or solar film?

Yes. We install anti-graffiti film over existing security or solar film. The anti-graffiti layer sits outermost and is replaced independently without disturbing underlying film.

Does anti-graffiti film change the appearance of the glass?

Standard clear film is virtually invisible. A slight sheen may be visible in direct sunlight at certain angles but there is no significant appearance change.

What surfaces can anti-graffiti film be applied to?

Film is designed for flat glass — windows, doors, mirrors, and glass partitions. For brick, concrete, metal, and signage we use permanent anti-graffiti coatings.
